Abstract: n. sp.
Author: Peter K. L. Ng
Title: Tuerkayana latens, a New Species of Land Crab from French Polynesia, with a Discussion on the Phylogeny of the Genus (Crustacea: Decapoda: Brachyura: Gecarcinidae)

Abstract: Abstract Selective hydrogenation of CO2 to propane and n-butane is of great interest, as these two compounds are not only primary components of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) but also crucial raw materials for preparing propene and a degradable plastic precursor of succinic acid. Although various composite catalysts combining metal oxides and zeolites have been explored, their catalytic performances remain insufficient. Here, we found that ZnZrOx decorated with ultrasmall FeOx clusters, forming an intimate FeOx–ZnZrOx interfacial structure, showed high catalytic activity for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol due to a strong CO2 adsorption capacity and H2 dissociation ability, and silicoaluminophosphate molecular sieve with RHO topological structure enhanced methanol conversion into propane and n-butane via hexamethylbenzenes as active hydrocarbon pool species owing to its unique supercage structure and double eight-membered ring pore opening. As a result, coupling of these two materials delivers a CO2 conversion of ∼66% and a (propane + n-butane) selectivity of 82% in hydrocarbons, which leads to a (propane + n-butane) yield of ∼42%. It is surprising that this composite preferentially produces n-butane rather than iso-butane, and the n-butane/iso-butane ratio is higher than 85.8. The high catalytic stability of this composite is demonstrated by maintaining CO2 conversion, (propane + n-butane) selectivity in hydrocarbons, and their yield of ∼ 61%, ∼ 77%, and ∼ 31%, respectively, after a reaction of 620 h. This work not only fabricates a high-performance catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation to propane and n-butane by engineering the metal oxide interfacial structure and manipulating the zeolite’s pore structure and acidity, but also makes it possible to develop an efficient way for preparing propene and succinic acid from CO2 hydrogenation.
Author: FAN, Yingnuo
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: Hydrogenation of CO2 to Propane and n -Butane by Engineering Metal Oxide Interfacial Structure and Manipulating Zeolite Pore Structure and Acidity

Abstract: Abstract Oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer is an important yet relatively underexplored elementary step in C–H functionalization. In this work, we employed cyclic voltammetry (CV) to measure the rates of hydride transfer between electrochemically generated oxoammonium catalysts and 42 substrates including ethers, carbamates, amides, and sulfonamides. Through quantum mechanical (QM) calculations, we uncovered a new transition-state model for hydride transfer in which the N atom of the catalyst resides near a heteroatom (X = N or O) of the substrate to allow alignment of the oxoammonium’s O═N+ motif and the substrate’s forming C═X+ bond. Energy decomposition analysis was subsequently performed to elucidate the key factors that govern the kinetics of oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer. Beyond conventional electronic and steric considerations, we identified substrate distortion, secondary orbital interactions, and noncovalent interactions as critical factors that influence hydride transfer reactivity. We anticipate that these kinetic data along with the mechanistic insights they provide will inform future catalyst development and synthetic applications to broaden the scope of oxoammonium catalysis.
Author: Kandahari, Elya
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: Electroanalytical and Computational Investigation of Oxoammonium-Mediated Hydride Transfer

Abstract: Abstract Circular RNA is a therapeutically promising RNA modality with superior stability and extended protein expression relative to linear RNA. While delivery systems for linear RNA have received much attention, less effort has been directed toward the delivery of circular RNA, whose closed topology and physicochemical properties differ from those of linear RNAs. Here, we disclose a class of ionizable lipids that enable efficient in vitro and in vivo delivery of circular RNA. These ionizable lipids are step-economically accessible, allowing facile assessment of their structure–delivery relationships. Our studies reveal key elements that enhance circular RNA delivery in vitro and in vivo, including aminoethoxy head units, doubly branched tails and linkers tuned for hydrogen bonding and biodegradability. The lead ionizable lipid for circular RNA delivery, iL-19, incorporating these features, achieves ∼28-fold higher protein expression in C2C12 myocytes than Moderna’s SM-102 formulation and 2.5-fold higher expression upon intramuscular administration in BALB/c mice. iL-19 also surpasses benchmark ionizable lipids ALC-0315 (7.8-fold) and DLin-MC3-DMA (33.4-fold) for intramuscular circular RNA delivery in vivo under otherwise identical conditions. This study establishes design principles and a step-economical synthesis for accessing ionizable lipids that enable highly efficient in vitro and in vivo circular RNA delivery.
Author: Cook, Adam
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: Circular RNA Delivery In Vitro and In Vivo Using Doubly Branched Aminoethoxy-Functionalized Ionizable Lipid Nanoparticles

Abstract: Abstract Developing active and durable water oxidation cocatalysts is essential for advancing photoelectrochemical (PEC) water-splitting systems. This study investigates the cesium-induced reconstruction of the FeOOH cocatalyst on a bismuth vanadate (BVO) photoanode for the water oxidation reaction, with a focus on the reconstruction process and its effect in improving interfacial charge transfer and photostability. Cesium ions induce the reconstruction of Fe species on the BVO/FeOOH photoanode during the PEC process, leading to the formation of a robust Cs-incorporated FeOOH (Cs:FeOOH) catalytic layer. Spectroscopic analysis combined with open-circuit potential measurement reveals that the in situ formed Cs:FeOOH cocatalyst can effectively protect BVO and promote interfacial hole transfer during PEC operation. As a result, the BVO/Cs:FeOOH photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 6.29 mA cm–2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE and maintains stable operation for over 100 h. Furthermore, the Cs-incorporated FeOOH cocatalyst strategy can be extended to other semiconductor systems, including TiO2 and FeOx, highlighting its broader potential for improving solar-driven PEC water oxidation.
Author: Jiang, Wenchao
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Subfield: Renewable Energy, Sustainability and the Environment
Title: Cesium-Induced Stabilization of the FeOOH Cocatalyst on Bismuth Vanadate Photoanode for Ultraefficient and Stable Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation

Abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) triggers a complex secondary injury cascade characterized by oligodendrocyte (OL) death and axonal demyelination, leading to permanent neurological deficits. Despite the presence of endogenous oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs), the inhibitory microenvironment-marked by inflammation, glial scarring, and biochemical barriers-prevents effective remyelination. Traditional pharmacological treatments are further hindered by the blood-spinal cord barrier and rapid clearance of intrathecal injections. This review examines the evolution of controlled release systems engineered to modulate the oligodendroglial lineage. We analyze macro- and micro-scale platforms, including scaffolds, which provide mechanical and topographical cues to direct the fate of OLs and OPCs. Furthermore, we discuss advanced nanoscale vectors, such as nanoparticles and exosomes, designed to deliver high-value payloads-including small molecules and therapeutic oligonucleotides-directly to the lesion site while minimizing systemic toxicity. Finally, we address critical translational gaps to bridge the divide between preclinical innovation and clinical application in restoring neural connectivity.
Author: Petillo, E.
Title: Biomaterial‐Based Controlled Release Systems for Spinal Cord Remyelination

Abstract: Phototheranostic agents operating in the second near-infrared (NIR-II) window hold great potential for precision cancer therapy, yet the rational regulation of excited-state processes to simultaneously optimize fluorescence and phototherapeutic performances remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report a topology-driven excited-state engineering strategy for constructing conjugated oligomers with tailored excited-state manifolds and multi-channel excitation dynamics. By precisely manipulating molecular topology, conjugated topological oligomers achieve enhanced light-harvesting capability and optimized exciton utilization, thereby enabling synergistic regulation of excitation dynamics. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, nanoparticles (NPs) derived from TBT-3 exhibit 2.8-fold enhanced NIR-II fluorescence brightness, 2.7-fold improved photothermal performance, and 7.5-fold increased total reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation compared with TBT-1. In vivo studies demonstrate that TBT-3 NPs enable high-resolution NIR-II fluorescence imaging and efficient tumor elimination. Moreover, TBT-3-mediated phototherapy induces immunogenic cell death and enhances antitumor immunity, leading to improved therapeutic efficacy when combined with anti-PD-1 immune checkpoint blockade. This work provides a molecular topology-based strategy for manipulating excited-state landscapes and establishes conjugated oligomers as versatile candidates for NIR-II phototheranostics and cancer immunotherapy.
Author: Yang, Yuliang
Title: Topological Engineering of NIR‐II Emissive Conjugated Oligomers With Unexpected Excited‐State Manifolds for Efficient Phototheranostics and Cancer Immunotherapy

Abstract: Brassica napus is a globally important allotetraploid oilseed crop with a complex genome and extensive structural diversity that remains incompletely characterized. Here, we present gap-free reference genome assemblies for Zhongshuang 11 (ZS11) and Westar, and assemble six additional accessions. We harmonize gene annotations across 22 genomes and develop BnaScope (https://rgmi.hzau.edu.cn/bnascope), a gene-centric functional genomics platform. Gene-based and graph-based pan-genomes identify 123,107 non-redundant gene clusters and 188,218 structural variants, including 112,417 transposable element-mediated structural variants (TEMSVs). TEMSVs show asymmetric distributions between An and Cn subgenomes and are associated with increased homoeolog expression imbalance, particularly for CDS-TEMSVs. SV-based genome-wide association analyses identify candidate genes underlying seed quality traits, and functional analyses demonstrate that BnaPYRDs negatively regulate seed glucosinolate content. These findings establish structural variation as an important contributor to homoeolog regulation and seed-quality variation in B. napus. This study develops a comprehensive pan-genome resource for Brassica napus and reveals how structural variations shape gene regulation and seed quality traits. The findings provide insights into genome diversity and crop improvement.
Author: Tan, Zengdong
Title: Transposable element-mediated structural variations shape gene expression and agronomic trait diversity in Brassica napus

Abstract: Abstract The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. Here we describe Infernogallus jamesi gen. et. sp. nov., a diminutive caenagnathid oviraptorosaur, and show that these theropods were specialised herbivores that originated alongside the rise of fleshy angiosperm fruits. The nearly complete, articulated skull of Infernogallus jamesi —the first for the clade—reveals drastic changes to the adductor musculature organisation, unique in non-avian theropods but converged upon by extant frugivorous parrots. These modifications enabled extensive oral processing of soft food using anteroposterior movement of the mandible and occlusion of ridges and grooves on opposed elements. Altogether, this attests to a highly specialised herbivorous diet in caenagnathids, which likely consisted in large part of fleshy angiosperm fruits, which increased in size and diversity in concert with the radiation of oviraptorosaurs. Caenagnathids thus provide one of the strongest candidates for angiosperm-based diet adaptations in dinosaurs, but their role in the Late Cretaceous proliferation of fruit—which shaped early Cenozoic flora—remains unclear.
Author: Gregory F. Funston
Title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda)

Abstract: Abstract Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact.
Author: Hsieh, Yi-Chen
Title: Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage

Abstract: Multimodal imaging of fluorescence and phase provides distinct and complementary insights into biological samples. Current multimodal techniques for simultaneous phase and fluorescent imaging primarily operate in transmission mode and are limited to thin samples, restricting their applications to bulky tissues and in vivo animals. While multiphoton microscopy has enabled deeptissue fluorescence imaging, integrating it with phase imaging remains challenging due to the limited availability of methods capable of reconstructing the 3D refractive index (RI) of bulky, label-free tissues in reflection mode at subcellular resolution. To bridge the technical gap, we develop fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography (FDT) that reconstructs the 3D RI of label-free objects from diffracted fluorescence images acquired in reflection mode under two-photon excitation. The RI reconstruction leverages the transport of intensity equation (TIE) and is solved by a self-supervised neural network based on explicit neural fields. Compared to the state-of-the-art implicit neural fields, the explicit neural fields significantly improve computational speed, reconstruction accuracy, and interpretability. Using FDT, we successfully reconstruct the 3D RI of a 300 µmthick label-free bovine myotube sample over a 530 × 530 µm2 field-of-view at subcellular resolution within 20 min. FDT is the first technique to extract 3D RI from diffracted fluorescence images in reflection mode for thick tissues, overcoming key limitations of existing multimodal systems. This work lays the foundation for broadly accessible, reflection-mode multimodal fluorescence-phase imaging in complex biological systems in the future.
Author: He, Ruiqing
Subfield: Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics
Title: Fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography using explicit neural fields

Abstract: Abstract Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is attractive for multiplex bioimaging owing to its excellent photostability and ultranarrow spectral bandwidth. However, achieving synergistic enhancement of excitation and Raman scattering fields remains challenging. Herein, the relationship between geometry and localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) was investigated by continuously tuning the aspect ratio (AR) of anisotropic Au nanopolyhedrons (Au NPHs). Central-body modulation while preserving sharp terminal tips enables continuous LSPR tuning while retaining tip-associated electromagnetic enhancement. The SERS behavior was further analyzed by considering the spectral matching between the LSPR and the excitation/scattering wavelengths. For different excitation wavelengths, the optimal SERS response can be achieved by selecting Au NPHs whose LSPR band best matches with the excitation and Raman scattering wavelengths. These results demonstrate that Raman enhancement is governed by spectral matching rather than a fixed optimal geometry. The optimized Au NPHs enabled the use of dual SERS probes for proof-of-concept multiplex biomarker imaging.
Author: He, Chaoqin
Title: Continuously Tunable Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance of Anisotropic Gold Nanopolyhedrons for Multiplexed Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Imaging
Topic: Gold and Silver Nanoparticles Synthesis and Applications

Abstract: Abstract Inefficient immune synapse formation limits the therapeutic efficacy of T cell-based immunotherapy in both solid tumors and hematological malignancies. Here, we report a fully synthetic, membrane-anchored dual-targeting aptamer engager, AptE 2, that acts as a programmable artificial immunological interface to redirect cytotoxic T cells toward cancer cells without genetic engineering. Constructed entirely from DNA aptamers through optimized bioorthogonal conjugation and enzyme-mediated ligation, AptE 2 integrates multivalent tumor recognition, T cell binding, enhanced nuclease resistance, and prolonged membrane anchoring within a single modular scaffold. In colorectal cancer models, AptE 2 promoted stable T cell–tumor cell engagement, enhanced cytotoxicity and cytokine secretion, and drove pronounced tumor regression with increased intratumoral CD8+ T cell infiltration and minimal systemic toxicity. Importantly, AptE 2 also demonstrated broad applicability in leukemia. In CCRF-CEM cells, AptE 2 exhibited strong surface binding, sustained membrane retention for up to 6 h, and superior resistance to wash-off compared with monovalent aptamers and bivalent controls. AptE 2-prearmed TALL-104 cells markedly enhanced leukemia cell clustering, increased cell lysis to over 90% under optimized coculture conditions, and amplified IFN-γ secretion. In a disseminated CCRF-CEM-Luc leukemia mouse model, AptE 2-mediated T cell therapy suppressed systemic leukemia progression, improved peripheral hematological profiles, and showed favorable tolerability without detectable major organ injury. These findings establish AptE 2 as a generalizable, nonprotein-based and nonviral immune engager platform for programmable T cell redirection across both solid and hematological cancers.
Author: Zhang, Chi
Title: Membrane-Anchored Dual-Targeting Aptamer Engagers for Programmable T Cell Redirection in Solid and Hematological Cancers

Abstract: Abstract Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) is a sustainable planning approach that integrates land use and transportation to promote compact, accessible, and efficient urban growth. However, in rapidly urbanizing metropolitan contexts, TOD assessment is often centered on planned station areas, while dense and historically established districts receive less attention despite their relevance for retrofit-oriented intervention. Addressing this gap, the originality of this study lies in developing a highly granular, multi-scalar GIS-MCDA framework to assess TOD retrofit and readiness potential across 413 administrative units (shiyakha) in the Greater Cairo Region. This approach combines literature-informed and expert-validated socio-economic, land-use, and transport indicators into a composite TOD Index. The framework integrates spatial normalization, hybrid weighting, and multi-criteria aggregation to generate a fine-grained map of TOD readiness that captures local variations in urban form and accessibility. The results reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity. Central districts such as Al-Sayeda Zainab, Bulaq, Azbakeya, Shubra, and Abdeen exhibit the highest TOD potential due to compact urban fabric, strong transit accessibility, and land-use diversity, whereas peripheral areas such as 15th May City, Tura, and Atfih show low suitability because of dispersed development, weaker infrastructure, and limited public transport coverage. The findings highlight the need to distinguish between consolidated districts requiring TOD retrofit and peripheral areas that demand longer-term structural transformation. Overall, the proposed framework offers a replicable decision-support tool to assist decision-makers and urban planners in prioritizing targeted interventions and infrastructure improvements, thereby guiding sustainable urban policy in rapidly growing metropolitan contexts.
Author: Elwan, Khaled
Title: Evaluation transit-oriented development potential using GIS-MCDA: “a spatial framework for Greater Cairo”

Abstract: Abstract Community empowerment is widely recognized as an effective strategy for improving resident satisfaction in the governance of cultural heritage sites. However, existing studies focus primarily on institutional design and do not systematically explore the underlying psychological conversion mechanisms. To fill this gap, this paper selects Baisha Ancient Town and Xijiang Qianhu Miao Village as cases, uses Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) to analyze data from 775 completed questionnaires, and explores the mediating effect of empowerment on residents’ satisfaction through cultural pride and community resilience. The results show that community empowerment not only directly promotes satisfaction, but also has significant indirect effects through emotional and institutional pathways, and the two show differences in different communities. Through unpacking the “institutional empowerment-psychological response-satisfaction feedback” process, this study contributes to theory by clarifying the synergistic roles of emotional and structural mechanisms and their contextual variations. Practically, it provides a governance framework that helps policymakers calibrate empowerment strategies to community development stages, thereby promoting both cultural continuity and socio-economic sustainability.
Author: Liu, Yujin
Title: Unpacking the institutional and psychological pathways of community empowerment in cultural heritage governance

Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to quantify posterior root volume loss and assess its association with posterior intrusion. Linear root length changes were also evaluated and compared with three-dimensional measurements. This retrospective single-arm study included 27 patients with anterior open bites treated with clear aligners. Cone-beam computed tomography scans obtained before and after treatment were analyzed. Volumetric and linear root changes of maxillary posterior teeth were measured, and intrusion was assessed relative to the palatal plane. Significant volumetric reductions were observed in selected molar and premolar roots, with the highest percentage loss in the palatal root of the maxillary left first molar. Linear reduction was minimal and significant only in one premolar. Posterior intrusion was limited and not statistically significant. Root volume loss was not associated with intrusion but showed correlations with age and treatment duration. Volumetric assessment detected changes not consistently identified by linear measurements.
Author: Aljahdali, Raghad
Title: Prevalence of posterior root resorption in open bite patients undergoing clear aligner treatment: a single-arm retrospective CBCT study

Abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG)-based biometrics have shown strong potential as an alternative authentication modality because ECG signals contain subject-specific cardiac morphology and provide inherent liveness information. However, recognition performance remains sensitive to signal noise, morphological variability, and detector-dependent R-peak localization errors, which may misalign segmented heartbeats and reduce feature consistency. This study proposes ConvWaveFormer , a hybrid wavelet and CNN-Transformer framework for ECG biometric identification. Following morphology-preserving preprocessing, fixed-length R-peak-centered heartbeats are processed through two branches. A Daubechies-4 wavelet branch captures multiresolution time-frequency information, while a residual 1D-CNN-Transformer branch learns local ECG morphology and within-heartbeat temporal dependencies. The deep and wavelet representations, together with their element-wise interaction, are fused to generate a compact biometric embedding. Margin-based supervision using ArcFace and CosFace further promotes intra-subject compactness and inter-subject separability. The framework was evaluated on ECG-ID, Heartprint, MIT-BIH Arrhythmia, and MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm using three R-peak detection and heartbeat segmentation methods: NeuroKit2, SciPy FindPeaks, and XQRS. Although the relative performance of the detectors varied across datasets, XQRS achieved the strongest or comparable overall performance in most cases and was therefore selected for the final five-fold evaluation. ConvWaveFormer achieved mean identification accuracies of 92.99%, 76.47%, 97.70%, and 99.63%, with corresponding EER values of 5.84%, 11.11%, 1.72%, and 0.34%, respectively. In cross-dataset evaluation, a three-source score-level ensemble achieved 87.35% Rank-1 accuracy, 6.09% EER, and 0.9808 ROC-AUC on ECG-ID without target-domain model retraining. These results demonstrate that ConvWaveFormer learns discriminative and transferable ECG representations across heterogeneous offline datasets. Nevertheless, strictly session-disjoint, cross-device, and continuous wearable evaluations remain necessary to establish robustness under unconstrained real-world conditions.
Author: Asif, Muhammad
Title: ConvWaveFormer: a hybrid wavelet and CNN-transformer framework for ECG biometric identification

Abstract: Intelligent decision-making frameworks need to be able to handle operational uncertainty, ambiguous expert judgments, and interactions among mission attributes to navigate and coordinate missions in an autonomous drone swarm efficiently. Traditional optimization and decision models do not effectively represent ambiguous expert judgments and critical navigation and coordination factors that impact the behavior of the systems in a nonlinear way. To overcome all these limitations, this study proposes a Picture Fuzzy Stepwise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis–VIšekriterijumsko KOmpromisno Rangiranje (PF-SWARA–VIKOR) framework for evaluating drone-swarm strategies under uncertain conditions. PF-SWARA weighting begins with an expert-based screening phase to determine the relevance of the criteria, allowing only the most relevant criteria to proceed to the weighting and ranking phase. Picture Fuzzy Sets (PFSs) provide a more complete representation of uncertainty and hesitation compared to ordinary or intuitionistic fuzzy sets by means of positive, neutral, negative, and refusal degrees that model expert ratings. While the criterion weights are obtained by PF-SWARA, the five strategies centralized, decentralized consensus-based, leader–follower, hybrid-adaptive, and behaviour-based reactive coordination strategies are ranked by PF-VIKOR. According to the hypothetical application, \({U}_{4}\) is the first preference, since it has the minimum compromise value \({\mathcal{Q}}_{4}=0.0000\) , and the preference order is \({U}_{4}\succ {U}_{2}\succ {U}_{1}\succ {U}_{5}\succ {U}_{3}\) . The most influential criteria are \({L}_{7}\) and \({L}_{1}\) , with weights of \(0.1360\) and \(0.1357\) , respectively. Furthermore, \({U}_{4}\) is first across all values of \(\tau =0.1 to 0.9\) , but the rankings in-between shift depending on the relative strength of the group's utility and the individual's regret. Since the case study uses simulated experts and hypothetical evaluations, the results are of methodological applicability and not empirically generalizable.
Author: Saadaoui, Kheir
Title: A picture fuzzy SWARA–VIKOR framework for evaluating drone-swarm navigation and mission-coordination strategies under uncertainty

Abstract: Using qualitative comparative analysis, our study draws on regulatory focus theory to examine how chronic promotion and prevention foci and situational factors are associated with reinvestment decisions in equity crowdfunding. Evidence suggests that both chronic promotion and prevention foci are sufficient conditions for reinvestment and that situational factors, particularly the absence of inhibitors related to information asymmetry, valuation difficulties, and exit constraints, play an important role. We also identify configurations incorporating the presence of inhibitor factors, which we interpret as consistent with investors adopting a speculative, bet-like approach. Our study offers practical insights for platforms and entrepreneurs by emphasising how transparent communication and risk disclosure can build investor trust and encourage continued investments.
Author: Civardi, Camilla
Title: Promotion and prevention regulatory focus in equity crowdfunding reinvestment decisions

Abstract: Increased access to finance is widely viewed as a key driver to increase adaptive capacity in response to climate change. However, apart from limited studies on borrowing behavior, little is known about how exposure to extreme heat is associated with microfinance clients’ financial behavior. This study addresses this gap by investigating the short-run associations of unusual heat with microfinance clients’ saving and withdrawal behavior. In a case study, it combines geo-located temperature data with a unique dataset of around 50,000 clients of a leading Microfinance Institution (MFI) in Benin. Applying two-way fixed effects, seemingly unrelated regression, and ordinary least squares models, the study finds that exposure to extreme heat is heterogeneously associated with microfinance clients’ financial behavior. Specifically, non-agricultural clients show suggestive evidence of the accumulation of precautionary savings after extreme heat days in the preceding quarter, while extreme heat days are negatively associated with agricultural clients’ savings. Microfinance clients increase their withdrawals when exposed to extreme heat within the preceding quarter, but the association is not robust for agricultural clients’ withdrawals in response to an increase in annual extreme heat days. Addressing the heterogeneous financial responses across different clients to extreme heat consequently requires explicit policy attention. Our findings contribute to a better understanding of the associations between extreme heat and individual economic outcomes, how financial behavior relates to weather risk, and how microfinance clients respond to shocks.
Author: Mader, Anna
Title: When heat hits: Short-run saving and withdrawal behavior among microfinance clients in Benin

Abstract: Cultivating Humulus lupulus L. under subtropical conditions is challenging because hops are adapted to temperate climates, where environmental factors influence plant development and secondary metabolism. This study evaluated the essential oil yield and chemical composition of cones and leaves from four hop varieties (Cascade, Columbus, Comet, and Nugget) cultivated under subtropical conditions in northwestern Paraná, Brazil. Essential oils were obtained by hydrodistillation and analyzed by GC–MS. Chemical variability was investigated using Pearson correlation, principal component analysis (PCA), and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA). Cascade and Columbus showed better agronomic performance, while Nugget and Comet produced the highest essential oil yields in cones (1.532% and 0.695%, respectively). In leaves, Nugget, Cascade, and Comet exhibited the highest yields. Sesquiterpene hydrocarbons predominated in most samples, with α-humulene and β-caryophyllene as major constituents in both organs. Oxygenated sesquiterpenes, including caryophyllene oxide and humulene oxides, were also identified in the essential oils. Phytol was relatively abundant in the leaves of Cascade, Columbus, and Nugget, demonstrating differences between vegetative and reproductive tissues. PCA revealed distinct chemical patterns among varieties and harvest periods, emphasizing the influence of genotype and seasonal conditions. These results demonstrate the potential of hop cultivation under subtropical conditions and highlight leaves as a promising source of volatile compounds for further valorization and industrial applications.
Author: Gabriela Catuzo Canônico Silva
Title: Analysis of the Chemical Profile of the Essential Oil from Leaves and Cones of Four Varieties of Humulus lupulus Cultivated in a Subtropical Climate Under Edaphoclimatic Conditions

Abstract: Abstract Childhood maltreatment (CM) is a risk factor for adult post-traumatic symptoms and white matter (WM) alterations. It remains unknown how WM microstructure is affected alongside two common military conditions, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI). Data from 299 participants (53% male, 35.69 ± 12.23 years of age) of the Injury and Traumatic Stress (INTRuST) clinical consortium was analyzed. The study included 56 individuals with PTSD (41 with comorbid mTBI), 107 with mTBI, and 136 controls (no PTSD and/or mTBI). Diffusion parameters (mean, axial, and radial diffusivity, MD, AD, RD; fractional anisotropy, FA) in major WM tracts were extracted from diffusion MRI. CM was assessed using the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ). Multiple regression models examined associations between CM severity and WM diffusion. Moderation analyses assessed the effect of PTSD and/or mTBI on these associations. Mediation analyses examined how WM diffusion affects the associations between CM and both PTSD and post-concussive symptom severity. Greater CM severity was associated with lower MD and AD, independent of PTSD and/or mTBI. WM diffusion, particularly in the corpus callosum and the superior longitudinal fasciculus, mediated the associations between CM severity and both PTSD (MD b ab = 0.022, AD b ab = 0.019-0.034) and post-concussive symptoms (MD b ab = 0.028-0.040, AD b ab = 0.032-0.047). Findings suggest that WM alterations are more strongly associated with CM itself than with either PTSD and/or mTBI. Mediating effects in regions critical for sensory integration highlight the role of WM microstructure as a neurobiological pathway through which CM might predispose to post-traumatic symptoms.
Author: Berger, Luisa
Title: The role of white matter microstructure in the association between childhood maltreatment and adult post-traumatic symptoms

Abstract: While texture modification ensures safe swallowing in dysphagia, homogeneous purees often compromise visual appeal. Treating shaping as the core design objective, this review evaluates established methods for engineering visual realism in pureed foods against available evidence, while explicitly identifying areas where evidence does not yet exist. Direct shaping methods are evaluated across IDDSI (International Dysphagia Diet Standardization Initiative) compliance, sensory acceptability, and practical implementation. Structural approaches that modify food structure rather than reshape purees are evaluated individually by mechanism and applicability due to limited evidence. Three-dimensional printing enables precise, automated deposition over manual piping, but faces throughput and formulation requirements that can complicate IDDSI compliance. Molding is accessible, but demolding remains challenging, and gelled formulations that facilitate demolding may fall outside IDDSI puree definitions. Shear gels may provide an alternative to continuous gelled matrices, although their deliberate use for shaping remains untested. Though not purees, enzymatically softened and transitional textures may yield cohesive, texture-modified states but require oral processing to form a bolus. Overall, these methods differed in their practical advantages and disadvantages, while swallowing-safety evidence remains generally limited. These conclusions inform food scientists, engineers and clinicians, whose collaboration is required to realize engineering visual realism within accessible dysphagia care.
Author: S. M. Goh
Source: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
Title: Engineering visual realism in pureed foods for dysphagia care

Abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Children aged 6-24 months are highly vulnerable to malnutrition during conflict because they depend on breastfeeding, complementary feeding and functioning nutrition services. This study assessed nutritional status, socioeconomic correlates, maternal knowledge and primary health care centre (PHCC) nutrition service gaps in Gaza. SUBJECTS/METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted at Al-Daraj Martyrs Health Centre, one of the remaining functioning PHCCs in Gaza City during the study period, between late August and October 2025. Mother-child pairs were recruited by convenience sampling. Of 276 mother-child pairs approached, 250 completed the questionnaire. The anthropometric analytic sample comprised 200 children with the required anthropometric information, while haemoglobin results were available for 55 of the 250 completed participants. RESULTS: Stunting affected 12.5% of children, underweight 20.1%, wasting 20.8%, and anaemia 63.6% of the haemoglobin-tested subsample. Underweight was associated with household food shortage (p = 0.013) and previous malnutrition treatment (p = 0.002), wasting with child age category (p = 0.0024), and anaemia with paternal unemployment (p = 0.020). Maternal knowledge and practice scores were positively correlated (r = 0.177, p = 0.012), but neither was independently associated with stunting or underweight in adjusted models. PHCC nutrition support was limited, with 71.0% of mothers reporting nurse-provided nutrition advice and 52.5% reporting growth-chart review. CONCLUSION: In this clinic-based sample from conflict-affected Gaza, malnutrition among children aged 6-24 months was substantial. The pattern suggests that nutritional risk was shaped more by structural deprivation and weakened PHCC support than by maternal knowledge alone. These findings underline the need to restore nutrition services and improve access to adequate food for young children.
Author: Murtaja, Lina
Title: Nutritional status and associated factors among children aged 6–24 months at a primary health care centre in conflict-affected Gaza

Abstract: This paper introduces and investigates a novel class of generalized almost history-dependent operators, which couple a linear instantaneous contraction with a Volterra-type memory integral term featuring time-dependent integrable kernels. The proposed framework provides a unified perspective that substantially extends classical history-dependent operators and naturally encapsulates standard fractional integral operators as canonical special cases. By employing suitably tailored weighted Bielecki-type norms, we rigorously establish the existence and uniqueness of fixed points for these operators in Bochner 𝐿 𝑝 spaces over finite time intervals. We systematically analyze three distinct classes of integrability conditions for the kernel functions, deriving the corresponding fixed point theorems via Young’s convolution inequalities. Furthermore, the abstract fixed point theory is successfully applied to resolve several concrete nonlinear physical models: bidirectionally coupled fractional evolution systems and dynamic frictional contact problems arising in viscoelasticity. These applications underscore the wide applicability and robust flexibility of our theoretical framework for analyzing complex evolutionary variational–hemivariational inequalities with memory effects.
Author: Liu, Zhenhai
Title: Fixed point theorems for generalized almost history-dependent operators and their applications

Abstract: Blood cortisol measurements may be confounded by sampling-induced handling and restraint, motivating the use of alternative matrices to assess adrenocortical activity in pigs. This narrative review examines the physiological time windows, collection requirements, analytical validation, and interpretive limitations of saliva, urine, feces, and hair. Saliva captures rapid responses but remains sensitive to collection conditions; urine integrates secretion over bladder filling and requires dilution correction; fecal glucocorticoid metabolites reflect delayed, integrated excretion and require a species-appropriate assay. Hair offers a potentially longer integration window, but controlled validation in pigs remains inconsistent, and clipping generally requires brief restraint. Antibody specificity, sample processing, and normalization constrain comparisons between studies. Published concentration benchmarks should not be interpreted as validated, production-stage-specific reference intervals. The practical matrix-selection framework presented here rests primarily on cross-study inference rather than direct comparisons of all four matrices under a common challenge. Cortisol indicates adrenocortical activation without establishing its cause or emotional valence. Interpretation therefore requires complementary behavioral, clinical, and production measures. A minimum reporting standard and priorities for paired-matrix validation, standardized sampling, and category-specific reference intervals are proposed. These matrices support comparative monitoring; none should be treated as a standalone diagnostic test of compromised welfare.
Author: Kovács, Levente
Title: Cortisol in Saliva, Urine, Feces, and Hair as Non- and Minimally Invasive Measures of Adrenocortical Activity in Intensively Housed Pigs
